properties.name: Exodus journey — main traditional path (schematic)
properties.short_blurb: Ordered path from Rameses exit through Yam Suph debate zone, traditional Sinai, Kadesh, and into the plains of Moab — not every EW-* camp.
properties.claim: Represents the biblical Exodus itinerary as a schematic route line linking published map nodes (Pi-Ramesses dig + selected EW wilderness stations + Moab/Jordan approach). It is a reading aid for Numbers 33 / Exodus narrative geography, not a surveyed trail.
properties.caveats: Many wilderness stations are traditional or unconfirmed (see EW layer confidence). Yam Suph crossing and Mount Sinai locations are actively debated — this main line uses the traditional Jebel Musa / southern Sinai packaging already on EW-15 and a representative Yam Suph pin (EW-07), not a proved GPS track. Do not treat intermediate bends as excavated roadbeds. Prefer showing debated alternate branches (Aqaba; NE Delta/Ballah) as separate optional features.

properties.caveats: This is a debated minority/popular packaging, not a scholarly consensus track. Nuweiba beach and Jabal al-Lawz lack the same excavated Egyptian fortress-chain context Hoffmeier stresses for the NE Delta. Include only as an honest alternate toggle so users see the debate — never label 'proved.'

properties.name: Assyrian deportation routes (Israel → Assyria; Judah campaign context)
properties.short_blurb: Schematic movement paths from northern kingdom fall (~722) and Judah/Sennacherib context toward Assyrian heartland — not a re-tell of Lachish dig alone.
properties.claim: Two related LineString segments: (A) Samaria fall deportation toward Halah/Habor/Gozan/Media destinations named in Kings; (B) Judah 701 campaign logistics axis Lachish↔Jerusalem with imperial hinterland toward Nineveh. Paths are corridor sketches, not caravan GPS.
properties.caveats: 2 Kings 17 names settlement regions (Halah; Habor/Gozan; cities of the Medes), not a single road with mileposts. Exact Halah location is uncertain. Sennacherib's 701 campaign is strongly documented at Lachish (reliefs + tell) but deportation volumes and routes for Judah differ from the northern exile. Do not merge 'Samaria fell' and 'Jerusalem delivered' into one undifferentiated arrow.

properties.short_blurb: Schematic Judah→Babylon movement for the 597 and 586 waves — corridor, not caravan GPS.
properties.claim: Represents deportation movement from Judah (Jerusalem / Lachish context) along the inland Levant–Euphrates corridor toward Babylon, with labeled segments for the 597 and 586 waves when UI needs them.
properties.caveats: Scripture gives waves and counts (e.g., Jeremiah 52) but not a surveyed path. Riblah appears as a Nebuchadnezzar headquarters locale in the narrative — approximate. Do not invent precise nightly camps. Babylon dig (BAB-01) and Daniel/Ezekiel prophet pins stay as sites; this is the path.

properties.name: Return from exile routes (Zerubbabel / Ezra / Nehemiah)
properties.short_blurb: Schematic Babylon/Susa → Jerusalem return paths for the main restoration waves — not precise caravan GPS.
properties.claim: Three related return features: Zerubbabel/Sheshbazzar wave from Babylon; Ezra's later return; Nehemiah's journey from Susa. Same inland corridor family, different narrative starts.
properties.caveats: Ezra–Nehemiah give months and staging notes (e.g., Ahava) but not dig-verified camps for every day. Ahava canal location is uncertain — omit fake precision. Susa start for Nehemiah is strong as a place (SUS-01) but the road is schematic. Cyrus decree context ties to CYR-01 findspot packaging without claiming the cylinder is 'the biblical scroll.'

properties.name: Holy Family early-life path (Bethlehem → Egypt → Nazareth)
properties.short_blurb: Event path for Matthew's flight to Egypt and return to Nazareth — endpoints reuse dig pins; no re-pinning Bethlehem/Nazareth.
properties.claim: Ordered tradition path: Bethlehem birth setting → Egyptian sojourn region → return to Nazareth, matching Matthew 2 narrative geography at atlas scale.
properties.caveats: Bethlehem and Nazareth have dig/tradition pins; the Egyptian sojourn site is not fixed archaeologically. Later Christian traditions cluster around Nile Delta / Old Cairo / Heliopolis districts — we use HEL-01 (Heliopolis) as a cautious regional waypoint, not a proved 'house of the Holy Family' dig. Do not invent a precise desert GPS track. Skip re-telling nativity dig details; this is the travel path.

properties.name: Passion Week path (Jerusalem sites connected)
properties.short_blurb: Ordered event path linking existing Jerusalem/NT pins — upper room tradition through Gethsemane, trial loci, Golgotha — as a path, not new digs.
properties.claim: A sequential Passion narrative LineString connecting published map pins (Bethany, Olivet/arrest, Temple approaches, Caiaphas ossuary locus, Golgotha) with honest traditional waypoints where dig pins are missing (upper room; praetorium; tomb packaging).
properties.caveats: Each stop has different certainty: Pool of Siloam / Pilgrimage Road archaeology is strong for Second Temple Jerusalem movement; Golgotha pin is traditional/contested packaging (Holy Sepulchre vs alternatives); Caiaphas pin is family ossuary findspot — not proven 'trial house'; Upper room (Cenacle) and Praetorium lack dedicated dig pins on our map; Garden Tomb vs Holy Sepulchre burial traditions remain debated. Path order follows Gospel sequence at tour scale — not a surveyed Via Dolorosa cadastral claim.

properties.name: Abraham migration path (Ur → Haran → Canaan → Egypt sojourn → return)
properties.short_blurb: Patriarchal migration schematic using excavated Mesopotamian/Levant nodes — honest mixed rating.
properties.claim: Schematic LineString for Genesis 11–13 migration geography: Ur toward Haran, into Canaan (Shechem/Bethel/Hebron regions), Egypt sojourn, return to the Negev/Canaan.
properties.caveats: Ur (UR-01) and many Canaan sites are excavated, but tying Middle Bronze / early second-millennium patriarchal dates to specific strata is debated. Haran has no dig pin on our map (OpenBible Harran coords). Egypt sojourn stop is regional (HEL-01/MEM-01), not a named Abraham house. Include because Scripture narrative + real sites exist — not because the path is 'proved GPS.'
